Here are the descriptions of the provided plots, following your guidelines:

The plots illustrate the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy metrics. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. 

The first line, representing “Final Accuracy”, is blue with circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 0.88 with a value of 0.83 and ends at 0.99 with a value of 0.86. The line generally remains between 0.82 and 0.87 across the x-axis, with a slight peak at 0.93 where the value reaches 0.87.

The second line, representing “Δ Accuracy”, is orange with diamond markers and a solid line style. It begins at 0.86 with a value of 0.25 and ends at 1.00 with a value of 0.23. This line demonstrates a decline from 0.25 to a low of approximately 0.17 at 0.94, then increases slightly to 0.23. 

The third line, representing “Initial Accuracy”, is green with square markers and a solid line style. It begins at 0.86 with a value of 0.77 and ends at 1.00 with a value of 0.85. This line shows a general increasing trend, starting at 0.77 and rising to 0.85, with a slight dip around 0.91 where the value is 0.81. Each line also includes error bars at each data point.
